ESPN Insider's Mike Sandow's alleged inside sources: Peyton might not get his job back (full text of article in comments)

FULL TEXT

No NFL team had won as many regular-season games as the Denver Broncos over the past three seasons. No team had scored as many points or gained as many yards. But general manager John Elway wanted more. In the offseason, he set in motion changes he thought would move the organization closer to its first championship since Elway was behind center 17 seasons ago. Head coach John Fox and his coordinators were out. Gary Kubiak and an all-star defensive staff were in.

What would it mean for 39-year-old quarterback Peyton Manning? The stated plan was for Kubiak to recreate the QB-friendly conditions that helped Elway win Super Bowls late in his career, when Kubiak was the team's offensive coordinator. And if the plan didn't work? The Broncos answered that question Tuesday when Kubiak announced backup Brock Osweiler would replace Manning as the starter against Fox's Chicago Bears in Week 11. Manning needs time to recover from various injuries, Kubiak said, but the reality is this move was a long time in the making. The bottom line for the Broncos is that they appear no closer to winning a championship even though their defense is sensational. Manning obviously would have been better off had the Broncos kept their offensive system in place, but as the $4 million pay cut he took before the season demonstrated, these changes were much bigger than him.

The switch to Osweiler brings to the fore potential endgame scenarios for Denver, none of which realistically includes Manning in a Broncos uniform next season. Insider views on the benching:

A personnel director I spoke with two months ago said he thought the Broncos would be eager to make the move to Osweiler at their earliest opportunity. They weren't going to move on from Manning outright, the thinking went, but they knew the end was near and wanted to see Osweiler in extended game action before the 2012 second-round pick played out the final year of his rookie contract.

"If anybody is going to make the change like that, the person who is going to do it is Elway," this director said. "No one else would do that in the middle of the season with possibly the greatest quarterback of all time. If stuff does not perk up, there will be a mystery injury and there will be no coming back."

The 0.0 passer rating and 0.1 Total QBR score Manning posted against Kansas City on Sunday removed the mystery from this decision. Manning has nine touchdown passes with 17 interceptions for the season after throwing 131 and 36, respectively, over his previous three years in Denver. Manning does appear to be hurt, but Kubiak cast Manning's injuries as bumps and bruises associated with the normal grind of an NFL season. The timing of this benching was politically comfortable.

"And, oh, by the way, you let Peyton break the all-time yardage record first," a longtime NFL executive observed. "You did right by him but are not doing any more."

Potential endgames for Broncos

Manning playing beyond this season isn't realistic given his age, performance trajectory and questionable fit for Kubiak's offense. The likeliest scenarios are clear: • Re-sign Osweiler as the starter: This becomes plausible if Osweiler plays well enough down the stretch to win the job. Tony Romo stuck with Dallas after making his starting debut in the second half of the 2006 season. Colin Kaepernick pulled it off with San Francisco in 2012. • Find a veteran starter: This sounds better in theory than in reality when one considers how few viable veterans are likely to reach the market. The Broncos could wind up liking Osweiler more than they like the veterans who hit the market. • Draft a potential starter: Denver will probably be picking toward the bottom of the first round. Even if the Broncos find a quarterback they like -- Mel Kiper Jr. lists potential top prospects here -- what are the odds of a rookie emerging as the starter right away? Not good.

What Osweiler brings to the table

Brock Osweiler will get his chance to start for the Broncos for the first time in his career. Joe Mahoney/AP The personnel director who foresaw the switch to Osweiler was not expecting Denver's offense to enjoy sustained success after the change. Until recently, the Broncos' offensive line was arguably more of a problem than Manning had been. Osweiler is taking over an offense that ranks 29th in expected points added per game after ranking no worse than fourth in any of the previous three seasons.

"I think they will still have the same issues," this director said, "but Osweiler is more athletic and more equipped to take some of the beating." Coaches and evaluators who studied Osweiler coming out of Arizona State differ in their assessments of him after only 54 regular-season pass attempts. "I think he is too tall," one evaluator said. "I do not think you can be 6-8 and be a good quarterback." A quarterbacks coach questioned whether Osweiler possessed enough quickness on multiple fronts. "I do not think he can process fast enough, and he does not possess a quick enough body to react," this coach said. "He can run the Kubiak offense, but the anticipation and the feel for the game and the instincts are not good enough to support the lack of quickness." An evaluator familiar with the Broncos described Osweiler as smart, exceedingly tough and a hard worker respected by teammates. He said Osweiler moves well and should become more accurate as he gets additional reps in practices and games. Asked about the quickness issues raised by the quarterbacks coach, a different offensive coach said he anticipated no serious troubles in that area. "That is such a progression offense in Denver that Osweiler will be all right," this coach said. The coaches and evaluators polled for this column thought the Broncos would be reluctant to make a switch back to Manning later in the season. "You have to commit to Osweiler," one evaluator said. "If you play him, you have to go with what he wants to do. Brock would have to really play bad for them to go back. He is a free agent at the end of the year. If he plays well enough, that could be an interesting situation. They can find out if he is a guy for the future. There is a lot going on there."
